text: curious, our bush approach looks like abad science project compared to this LMFAO is there anything we can gain for our bush and green parts of a tree
resolution: Took over the bush TILE with the grass card-population approach and retired the ugly solid-sphere bush prop. Generalized render3d/grassPopulation into one populateFoliage(world, spec) roll driven by a FoliageSpec (config + tile→density-level map); grass and bush are two specs (rule of two, no duplicate roll). Added BUSH_CONFIG (taller/wider/denser leafier clumps, own greens) registered as its own 'bush' /settings tunable group (height/density/ColorWheel, same rig). New BushClump geometry (runtime/geometries): 5 cards fanned a full circle, tips splayed OUTWARD so it reads as a leafy shrub, not a tuft. BushField (GrassField.tsx, shared FoliageField inner) renders it through the same '~grass~' foliage pipeline (wind+cutout+gradient), wired into WorldStatics. Compiled parity: world_loader.zig SHAPE_BUSH=7 + buildBushClump() + bucket + static node + streaming family/proto (tex_key '~grass~', whitened-skip already covers it); worldGeometry pushFoliage() emits grass+bush. Retired the 'bush' prop from the scatter forest brush + the nature palette (def left dormant). Verified: editor bundle + ship + self-shot PASS; rjit game shot PASS (grass 19344 + bush bakes; bush 0 only because the saved map has no bush painted yet). Trees (canopy cards, lifted higher) are the next slice the user flagged. Not committed (shared files).
